newsitem.title: USA: SEC reaches out, halts trading on bulletin board.
newsitem.headline: SEC reaches out, halts trading on bulletin board.

text.p: The government's securities sleuths are getting smarter -- and faster -- in alerting the public about potential problems affecting a traded stock.

This morning, the Securities and Exchange Commission ordered the trading suspension of Omnigene Diagnostics Inc., citing questions raised about the accuracy of publicly disclosed information about the company.

Per procedure, the agency issued the usual press release and posted the investor alert on its Internet Web site, www.sec.gov. But it took a further step to expand its reach and get more people to know about the suspension.
It tapped the services of America Online, the nation's largest online service with about 7 million subscribers, by posting a message about the suspension on AOL's message board.
An SEC spokesman said the agency used the same bulletin board on AOL where Omnigene disseminated information about its operations to alert the public about the suspension.
"This way, the people who read OmniGene's information will also learn about what the SEC has found out," the spokesman said.

William McLucas, SEC's enforcement chief, said while the SEC normally uses its Web site to seek information about securities fraud, it will now be using the Internet to alert investors about potential problems affecting specific securities "when circumstances warrant."
"This is the first time we've done so, but it will not be the last," he said.

The trading suspension on OmniGene, a producer of DNA probe-based test for the detection of periodontal disease, became effective Wednesday morning and will last through December 4, the commission said.

The temporary suspension arose from the company's alleged ownership and other rights to certain patents and trademarks, past and projected sales, operations and facilities, and the number of freely traded shares of stock.
Omnigene president Dominic Scacci, in a statement, said his company will be working to address the SEC's concerns.
"I can assure everyone that as soon as we know exactly what information the SEC is requesting, we will forward the necessary documents and attempt to rectify the situation."
